localChanges: The map used to hold a full-size copy of the whole world for every layer it draws — seven of them, over a hundred and thirty megabytes before a single tile appears, and more again on a bigger map. Each layer is now only as big as the window you are looking through, which hands back about ninety-five megabytes and stops the cost growing with the map (#7).

It redraws only the part of the screen that actually changed, too. Scrolling moves the picture it already has and fills in the strip coming into view, and the unit waiting for orders blinks by repainting its own tile instead of the entire map.
Resizing the window could leave the map blank until something else happened to redraw it. It comes straight back now.
